factual_errors.claim: 'The PLC is likely still expecting DH-485... while the USR-N540 is sending plain Ethernet-TCP/IP packets, so the PLC never sees a valid DH-485 response.'
factual_errors.why_wrong: Mischaracterizes the failure mode: the USR-N540 is configured as a transparent RS-485-to-Ethernet converter, so on the RS-485 side it is passing raw bytes, not necessarily 'plain Ethernet-TCP/IP packets' reaching the PLC. More importantly, it omits the real reason a transparent converter can never work here — the absence of DH-485 token-passing arbitration and TX-EN half-duplex control, which no amount of protocol/mode matching fixes.

factual_errors.claim: First checks: verify the PLC's communication module is still set to DH-485 mode (baud, parity, stop bits) and confirm the USR-N540 is in 'transparent' mode.
factual_errors.why_wrong: Presents the issue as a configuration mismatch to be tuned. A transparent converter is structurally incapable of DH-485 arbitration regardless of how correctly baud/parity/mode are set, so this framing can send a technician down a multi-hour dead end.

factual_errors.claim: 'Use a handheld RS-485 sniffer or oscilloscope (de-energized side) to see whether the PLC is actually transmitting DH-485 frames and whether the converter is passing them unchanged.'
factual_errors.why_wrong: Reasonable in principle, but is offered as a diagnostic step rather than pointing at the definitive fix; a technician following this playbook could confirm the byte-level pass-through works and still never realize a transparent converter cannot support multi-drop DH-485 arbitration.

factual_errors.claim: (Omission) No statement that the correct resolution is to reinstall the protocol-aware interface or use an equivalent device (1747-AIC / 1761-NET-AIC); no mention of the DH-485 RJ45 port's non-Ethernet voltage levels and the equipment-damage risk of miswiring it.
factual_errors.why_wrong: Both are the two highest-value facts for this exact swap scenario and are absent.

notes: Same defects as the machine_selected condition, delivered with equal confidence and zero citations (manual_search was skipped entirely in new_chat mode). The answer is internally coherent and its individual troubleshooting steps (LOTO, wiring polarity/termination, protocol-mode check) are safe, but it never surfaces the one governing fact — that DH-485 token-passing arbitration and TX-EN control cannot exist on a transparent converter no matter how it's configured — and instead leads with steps that cannot resolve the fault. No hedge, no citation, no acknowledgement that this is general reasoning rather than sourced fact. Fails the correctness floor and is essentially unsupported for a fully asset-specific troubleshooting recommendation.
